h1:
Samut Prakan Blanched Cockles
Best Spots in Paknam & Bang Pu
intro: Samut Prakan sits right on the inner Gulf of Thailand, so the cockles here reach your plate fresh and plump, with juicy red meat. Blanched just to the point of done and dipped in a punchy seafood sauce, they keep you slurping all day. We've rounded up the spots that locals in Paknam and Bang Pu actually eat at, plus market stalls where you can buy cockles to blanch at home.

blocks.html: When people talk about food in Samut Prakan, blanched cockles are the first thing that comes to mind for a lot of them. The province sits at the mouth of the Gulf of Thailand, and the Bang Pu and Paknam areas get cockles brought in every day. Most places blanch them with the timing dialled in so the meat stays red and springy, never cooked until tough, then serve them with a sour-spicy-salty seafood dip that each shop makes its own way. We've picked spots that are actually open and that locals bring up often, and we'll tell you straight what each one is best at.

blocks.text: Cockle & seafood spots locals in Paknam and Bang Pu actually go to

items.name: Rim Khuean Seafood (the old shop), Paknam
items.blurb: A long-running shophouse in the Paknam area, tucked in a soi near the city observation tower and Paknam BTS. The setting is no-frills, but the seafood is fresh and the seafood dip is bold — it's kept locals coming back for years. Plump blanched cockles, blue swimming crab som tam, and tom yum grouper are the regulars' go-to orders.

items.name: Ao Bang Pu (seaside spot in Bang Pu)
items.blurb: A waterfront spot in the Bang Pu area with a cool sea breeze, quick service, and prices that won't sting. People praise the fresh blanched cockles and big oysters, and the steamed crab is great too. Good for settling in over a long family meal, with decent parking.
items.meta: Bang Pu seafront · 2 zones · easy parking

items.name: Pho Thale, Bang Pu
items.blurb: Shady open-air seating with a view over the Bang Pu area, all about a relaxed vibe. Blanched cockles, sea bass fried with fish sauce, and crab fried rice are the frequent orders. Plates run roughly 100–450 THB.
items.meta: Bang Pu · outdoor seating · ~100–450 THB per plate

items.name: Hoy Lung Lek, Paknam
items.blurb: A spot reviewers single out for freshness — the owner happily lets you taste first if you're unsure. Blanched cockles are the star here: firm, easy to shuck, and great for anyone who wants to focus on the cockles rather than a fancy setting.
items.meta: Paknam area · all about fresh catch

items.name: Somphong Seafood
items.blurb: An old-timer running for over 20 years, passed from father to son. Cockles, fresh oysters, and sea bass fried with fish sauce are the signatures. Locals trust it for freshness and a steady hand in the kitchen that hasn't wavered in years.

items.name: Nai Ma's
items.blurb: A seafood spot Samut Prakan locals know. Spicy cockle salad (yum hoy khraeng) and seafood tom yum are the standout dishes. Plenty of parking, good for getting together with a group or a big family.
items.meta: lots of parking · good for groups

blocks.title: Order smart
blocks.html: If you're with a few people, order one plate of blanched cockles and tell the staff how done you like them — red and springy (lightly blanched) or just cooked through with no blood. Many shops will blanch them to your liking. Then add seafood tom yum and sea bass fried with fish sauce as your mains; that works out better value than ordering only cockles.

blocks.text: Buy fresh cockles to take home — Paknam Market

blocks.html: If you want to eat cheap and control the doneness yourself, Paknam Market is where locals go for fresh cockles. The market is in town on the bank of the Chao Phraya River, near Paknam BTS, and seafood there isn't pricey. There are several cockle stalls to choose from — buy a batch to blanch at home and you'll get them fresher and cheaper than eating out.

items.name: Je Ang Home Cockles
items.blurb: A cockle stall in Paknam Market handling both wholesale and retail. Well known among market regulars — ask the vendor to pick out the plump ones for you.

items.name: Je Pan (Pak Daeng)
items.blurb: A small cockle stall in Paknam Market that reviewers mention for freshness. Buy a batch to blanch at home.

blocks.title: How to pick plump cockles
blocks.html: Fresh cockles have shells clamped shut, or if open, they snap shut when you touch them. Any that stay open are dead — toss those. Back home, soak them in water with a splash of vinegar for about 10 minutes to purge the grit; any that float to the top are no good, so pick those out before blanching.

blocks.text: Blanch them at home — tasty, no fishy smell

items: Rinse and soak first — scrub the shells clean and soak in water with a splash of vinegar for about 10 minutes to purge the grit. They'll shuck more easily and won't smell fishy after blanching.

Watch the timing — drop the cockles in once the water is boiling; about 1 minute gives you just-cooked, soft and springy meat, dry blood, no fishy smell. If you like them red and springy, cut the time down.

Easy seafood dip — pound green and red bird's eye chilies, garlic, and coriander root together, then season with fish sauce, lime juice, and a little sugar. Taste it: sour leading, spicy following, salty-sweet in balance.
Serve right away — blanched cockles are best while still warm; shuck, dip, and eat. Leave them too long and the meat turns tough and loses that juicy taste.

blocks.text: When to go and how to get there

blocks.html: Most seafood spots in the Paknam area open from evening into the night. If you're heading to Bang Pu, late afternoon into evening is the sweet spot for the sea breeze and sunset. Paknam is easy to reach on the BTS Green Line — get off at Paknam station and take a short ride from there. Bang Pu is easier to drive to, with parking at the seaside spots. Weekends get busy, so leave a little time for a table.

faq.q: Where's good to eat blanched cockles in Samut Prakan?
faq.a: The Paknam area has old-timers like Rim Khuean Seafood and Hoy Lung Lek that focus on fresh catch, while around Bang Pu you've got Ao Bang Pu and Pho Thale where you can sit by the sea with a cool breeze. Pick based on whether you want an old shop's cooking or a seaside vibe.

faq.q: Are Samut Prakan cockles really fresh?
faq.a: The province sits on the inner Gulf of Thailand, and the Bang Pu and Paknam areas get cockles brought in every day, so most spots have fresh stock. To be sure, look for places locals frequent, or buy from a stall in Paknam Market and blanch them yourself.

faq.q: Where can I buy fresh cockles to take home?
faq.a: Paknam Market in town on the bank of the Chao Phraya River, near Paknam BTS, has several cockle stalls like Je Ang and Je Pan at fair prices. Just ask the vendor to pick out the plump ones for you.

faq.q: How do I blanch cockles at home without the fishy smell?
faq.a: Soak them in water with a splash of vinegar for about 10 minutes first to purge the grit, then blanch in boiling water for about 1 minute so the meat is soft and springy with the blood set. Don't overdo it, or the meat turns tough and loses its flavor.

faq.q: What time do Paknam seafood spots open?
faq.a: Many places in the Paknam area open in the evening, around 16:00 until about 22:00. Seaside spots in Bang Pu usually open from afternoon into the night. Weekends get busy, so leave a little time for a table.
